title: Choose the visual world — bolder hand
question: You asked for more of that creative energy. Six foreign forms, full commitment, no safe pick this round — lock one in, or re-roll again.

options.label: Composable Systems
options.thesis: Her skills as independently-tensioned color bands that overlap into named composite states — a systems thinker rendered as visible composability.
options.viewport: A full-bleed sunlit courtyard: three translucent banners (Backend, Leadership, Shipped Work) cross overhead, each overlap labeled with the real credential it produces — e.g. Backend × Leadership = AIESEC QA Lead — CTA sitting in the one clear-sky gap.
options.risk: Gorgeous and genuinely unique, but the composability metaphor only works if every overlap is labeled in words, not color alone — otherwise a fast-skimming recruiter reads mood instead of meaning.

options.label: Load-Bearing
options.thesis: Her experience as a tensegrity structure — every claim is a rod held up by a named, traceable counterforce, the whole column visibly breathing under load.
options.viewport: A floating column of carbon-rod nodes (roles, projects) held apart by red tension cords labeled with real figures — GPA, years, projects shipped — the column slowly lengthening on scroll as more load joins.
options.risk: Risks reading as an engineering-diagram gimmick unless every 'force' label carries a real, verifiable fact rather than decorative physics jargon.
options.case: Beats the leader on both axes: force diagrams and monospace annotations read as engineering at a glance, and a load/counterforce model maps directly onto dependency and capacity thinking — the backbone of backend work.

options.label: Man-Machine Interface
options.thesis: Her as a wiring diagram of a man-machine system — every role and project a node, every connection a live traffic-signal state: green shipped, amber in progress, red retired.
options.viewport: A black traffic-grid field: geometric nodes for each credential wired together with neon connector lines, red/amber/green states lighting each node — the current internship glowing live green — her name set in tight tracked caps as the page's one banner line.
options.risk: The closest of the hand to a literal system-architecture diagram — if the wiring gets too dense it reads as a subway map instead of a resume; every node needs one unmistakable, skimmable label.
options.case: Beats the leader on both axes: traffic-signal states are a universal, instantly legible status convention even to non-technical recruiters, and the wiring-schematic form is literally how she'd draw the systems she builds — the strongest single alternate in this hand.

options.label: Instrumented
options.thesis: Her track record as a bank of glowing lab counters — GPA, years shipped, projects live, each metric a physical, countable digit.
options.viewport: A row of nixie-tube digit banks across a dark steel panel, each tube counting up to a real number on load, an engraved caption beneath each bank naming the metric.
options.risk: Strong on memorability and metric display, weaker at explaining anything that isn't a number — the RBAC/systems-design story needs its own section outside the counter bank.
options.case: Holds audience identification — nixie tubes read instantly as engineering instrumentation — but doesn't stretch as far as the leader into explaining how her systems actually work; competitive, not a clean win.

options.label: The Queue
options.thesis: Her experience rendered as a literal processing queue — depth is rank, the frontmost brightest line is active now (the internship), everything behind drifts at its own pace.
options.viewport: An emissive black void with one bright bitmap line at the front (current role), older roles and projects receding into dimmer, smaller, drifting layers behind it, an amber caret blinking at the head.
options.risk: The demoscene/cracktro reference is a real technical in-joke — queues and depth read fast to programmers, but this is the highest audience-recognition risk in the hand for a non-technical HR screener.
options.case: Product clarity is excellent — a queue is a literal backend primitive, and depth-as-rank cleanly prioritizes the current internship — but identification is narrower than the leader's; competitive, not a clean win.

options.label: Permission Lattice
options.thesis: Her role-based systems drawn as a punched silver lattice — every cell a permission, filled solid where access is granted, pierced open where it isn't.
options.viewport: A strict black-ruled white gallery grid, each square cell one permission (admin / staff / member × feature) from MOVEHAUS's real access model, filled or pierced accordingly, framed like showroom metalwork.
options.risk: Elegant and precise, but the luxury-showroom material (hammered silver, gallery lettering) reads more design/craft than software — the clearest way this hand could land as too refined rather than too playful.
options.case: Wins product clarity decisively — the punched grid is a literal, checkable diagram of the RBAC feature she actually shipped — but loses identification against the leader: recruiters read 'luxury goods showroom' before they read 'engineer.'

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The clean modern developer-portfolio template, executed impeccably instead of played safe.
canonCard.viewport: A centered hero card, section grid below, the arrangement any recruiter has seen a hundred times — at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other student portfolio by design — the exact 'too corporate/safe' outcome flagged as the one to avoid.
